scenario:
A PROPOSED RESTAURANT PLAZA ON A PROJECT SITE HAVING AN 8.0% SLOPE

Statement of the problem: A development company has decided that its newly acquired property, with a total lot area (TLA) of 4,500 sqm, shall be developed to host a restaurant plaza (the "Project"). The property is zoned C-2 and is located in one of the better parts of Pasig City (the "Project Site").

• A front setback 17.0 m deep shall be provided to accommodate a parking lot at the front of the property.
• Each side of the lot shall have a 5.0 m-wide setback, while the rear shall have a 6.0 m-wide setback. The side and rear setbacks shall be used as driveways around the building.
• The project shall be a one-storey restaurant plaza with an outdoor dining area at the front and eight (8) enclosed kitchens at the rear to accommodate eight (8) tenants.
• There shall be a 3.0 m-deep sidewalk at the front of the building, parallel to the RROW. This sidewalk shall be part of the 17.0 m front setback.
• The sidewalk shall lead to a 6.0 m-deep outdoor dining area in front of the enclosed kitchens. This dining area shall be one continuous strip, with no permanent partitions separating one tenant's dining area from another's.
• The remaining 16.0 m-deep area at the rear shall be subdivided into eight kitchens arranged side by side. Each kitchen shall be enclosed, with an access door at the front and a service door at the rear accessible from the driveway. Fenestrations shall be provided on each kitchen's front and rear sides only.

For greater market acceptance, the minimum parking requirements of the 2004 Revised IRR of PD 1096 (NBCP) should be exceeded, and parking shall be positioned at the front area.

Project site features: The site is a rectangular inside lot with a 100.0 m-wide frontage. Provide a 5.0 m-wide driveway on both sides and a 6.0 m-wide service driveway at the back. The site uniformly slopes at 8.0% towards a 20.0 m-wide RROW in front. The RROW has 2.40 m-wide sidewalks on each side. The surface of the sidewalk adjoining the front of the lot is taken as elevation 0.0 m. To the left of the site is a private high school building; to its right is a residential condominium building; to the rear are proposed three-storey single-detached residences.

Design objectives: (a) to design a restaurant plaza that is marketable and attractive to middle-income renters/lessees; (b) to design the restaurant building so that it maximizes rentals and leases for the developer; and (c) to design a building that will serve as a landmark in the project area, with sustainable plan/design features, deliverable at the least cost.

q: Trims and moldings are
n: Trims and moldings are finish woodwork produced in a planing mill, so they are classed as millwork. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated, Ch. 10 (Finish Work – Millwork); Max Fajardo, Simplified Construction Estimate.

q: What is the minimum area required by the NBC for kitchens?
n: Sec. 806 sets the minimum kitchen size at 3.00 sqm, with a least dimension of 1.50 m. Source: 2004 Revised IRR of PD 1096 (NBCP), Rule VIII, Sec. 806 (Size and Dimensions of Rooms).

q: What is the minimum dimension required by the NBC for kitchens?
n: Sec. 806 sets the minimum least dimension of a kitchen at 1.50 m (minimum area 3.00 sqm). Source: 2004 Revised IRR of PD 1096 (NBCP), Rule VIII, Sec. 806.

q: What is the occupant load prescribed by the NBC for kitchens?
n: The NBC occupant load table assigns 18.60 sqm per person to commercial kitchens. Source: 2004 Revised IRR of PD 1096 (NBCP), Rule XII, Table XII.1 (Occupant Loads – Kitchens, commercial).

q: Where should the accessible parking slot be located?
n: Accessible parking slots must be located nearest to the accessible building entrance, so that the route to the door is as short as possible. Source: BP 344 (Accessibility Law) IRR, Rule II – Parking Areas; BP 344 2024 Revised IRR.

q: A turnabout space should be provided outside toilet stalls for PWDs. How big should this turnabout space be?
n: A turnabout space of at least 2.25 sqm, with a minimum dimension of 1.50 m, is provided for a wheelchair to turn around. Source: BP 344 (Accessibility Law) IRR, Rule II, Minimum Requirements – Corridors and Toilets.

q: According to the NBC, which occupant load applies to commercial kitchens?
n: The NBC occupant load table lists commercial kitchens at 18.60 sqm per person. Source: 2004 Revised IRR of PD 1096 (NBCP), Rule XII, Table XII.1.

q: According to RA 9514, what is the maximum riser height for new stairs?
n: The Fire Code sets a maximum riser height of 180 mm (and a minimum tread of 280 mm) for new stairs. Source: RA 9514 (Fire Code of the Philippines) 2019 RIRR, Div. 10.2.5 (Means of Egress – Stairs).

q: If you subtract the ISA from the MACA, what will you get?
n: MACA = PSO + ISA, so MACA − ISA = PSO. Source: 2004 Revised IRR of PD 1096 (NBCP), Rule VIII, Table VIII.1, note c.

q: What is the difference in height between the highest and lowest points of the lot?
n: Lot depth = 4,500 / 100 = 45 m. Rise = 8% × 45 m = 3.60 m. Source: basic site grading (slope = rise / run); De Chiara & Koppelman, Time-Saver Standards for Site Planning.

q: Based on the NBC guidelines, which shall be considered the established grade elevation when measuring building height if the edges of the building footprint running perpendicular to the RROW differ in elevation by more than 3.0 m?
o: The lowest elevation of the lot
The finish floor level of parking lot
The highest elevation of the lot
The average between the lowest and highest elevations of the lot
n: Where the edges of the footprint perpendicular to the RROW differ in elevation by more than 3.00 m, the average grade level of the lot is taken as the established grade. Source: 2004 Revised IRR of PD 1096 (NBCP), Rule VII, Table VII.2, note a (Establishing Grade).

q: In order to satisfy the parking provisions required by the NBC, the project may make use of a permanent parking building if the said building is how far from the project?
o: No more than 100.0 m away from the project
All parking provisions must be provided on-site
No more than 200.0 m away from the project
No more than 50.0 m away from the project
n: Parking may be provided in a permanent parking building located no more than 200.00 m away from the office or commercial project. Source: 2004 Revised IRR of PD 1096 (NBCP), Rule VII, Sec. 707, Table VII.4 notes.

q: For deliveries, the owner asked you to provide parking slots for three delivery trucks. What are the minimum dimensions required by the NBC for standard trucks?
n: A standard truck or bus parking/loading slot is computed at a minimum of 3.60 m × 12.00 m. An articulated truck slot is 3.60 m × 18.00 m. Source: 2004 Revised IRR of PD 1096 (NBCP), Rule VII, Sec. 707, item 4.

q: How big should a circular dining table be in order to seat 8 people?
n: A round table about 60 in (1.50 m) in diameter seats 8 diners comfortably, at about 600 mm of perimeter per person. Source: Panero & Zelnik, Human Dimension and Interior Space (Dining); Neufert, Architects' Data (Restaurants).

q: What is the ideal dining table height for comfortable dining?
n: Standard dining table height is about 730–760 mm, so 750 mm is the comfortable height. Source: Panero & Zelnik, Human Dimension and Interior Space; Neufert, Architects' Data.

q: What is the ideal seat height for comfortable dining?
n: A dining chair seat height of about 430–460 mm (around 450 mm) suits a 750 mm table. Source: Panero & Zelnik, Human Dimension and Interior Space; Neufert, Architects' Data.

q: For busy commercial kitchens, what countertop finish would you recommend if ease of cleaning and low maintenance requirement are primary concerns?
n: Stainless steel is non-porous, resists heat and corrosion, and is easy to sanitize. That is why it is the standard surface for commercial kitchens. Source: Time-Saver Standards for Building Types (Restaurants – Kitchen Design); FDA Food Code (food-contact surfaces).

q: What needs to be installed in the kitchen to keep cooking oils and other similar contaminants from entering the public drainage system?
n: A grease trap (interceptor) holds back fats, oils and grease from kitchen waste before the waste enters the drainage system. Source: Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Sec. 1011 (Grease Traps and Interceptors).

q: What constitutes the work triangle in a kitchen?
n: The kitchen work triangle links the three main work centers: refrigerator (storage), cooktop (cooking) and sink (cleaning). Source: Time-Saver Standards for Housing and Residential Development (Kitchens); Neufert, Architects' Data.

q: What paint color would you recommend if the restaurant owner desires to increase the turnover rate of diners (decrease the time spent by customers inside the restaurant)?
n: Bold, bright warm colors are stimulating and speed up turnover, which is common in fast-food interiors. Cool and neutral colors encourage people to linger. Source: Mahnke, Color, Environment and Human Response; Ching, Interior Design Illustrated (Color).

q: It is a movable shelter supported entirely from the exterior wall of a building and of a type which can be retracted, folded or collapsed against the face of a supporting building. Its horizontal clearance from the curb line shall not be less than 300mm and the vertical clearance from its under most surface and the pavement or ground line shall be not less than 2.40m.
n: NBC Sec. 1006 defines a movable awning (hood) as a retractable or folding shelter supported entirely from the exterior wall. It must clear the curb line horizontally by at least 300 mm and have at least 2.40 m vertical clearance. Source: 2004 Revised IRR of PD 1096 (NBCP), Rule X, Sec. 1006 (Movable Awnings or Hoods).

q: Many customers of an enclosed restaurant and bar complain about too much noise in the space. Which option can be recommended to the owner?
o: Remove the wood paneling on the walls and expose the concrete surfaces
Add soft materials like carpets and drapery
Add mirrors on some of the walls
Increase the lighting of the space
n: Soft, porous materials such as carpets and drapery absorb sound and cut reverberation. Hard surfaces, mirrors and lighting do nothing to reduce noise, or make it worse. Source: Egan, Architectural Acoustics; Stein & Reynolds, Mechanical and Electrical Equipment for Buildings (Acoustics).

q: A full (double) size bed is
n: A full (double) bed mattress is about 54 in × 75 in (137 × 190 cm). Source: Panero & Zelnik, Human Dimension and Interior Space; Time-Saver Standards for Interior Design (Bed Sizes).

q: The base of the Pyramid of Khufu is
n: The Great Pyramid of Khufu at Giza stands on a nearly perfect square base about 230 m on each side. Source: Fletcher, A History of Architecture (Ancient Egypt); Fazio, Moffett & Wodehouse, A World History of Architecture.

q: An act authorizing the Ministry of Human Settlements to establish and promulgate different levels of standards and technical requirements for economic and socialized housing projects in urban and rural areas.
n: BP 220 (1982) authorized the Ministry of Human Settlements to set and promulgate different levels of standards and technical requirements for economic and socialized housing projects in urban and rural areas. Source: Batas Pambansa Blg. 220 and its Revised IRR (HLURB, 2008).

q: During construction, you noticed a colony of termites. What will you do to prevent a future termite infestation?
o: Use pest-control products upon completion of the building
Hire a termite control service contractor
Apply termite poison on the building's foundation and the perimeter or where there is contact with the soil
Use agricultural chemicals on the soil
n: Soil poisoning (anti-termite soil treatment) at the foundation and along the perimeter where the building touches the soil creates a chemical barrier against subterranean termites. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated, Ch. 3 (Termite Protection); NSCP/DPWH specifications on soil poisoning.

q: For a warehouse-factory, which would you recommend for partitions?
n: Warehouse-factory partitions take impact, moisture and fire exposure. CHB masonry is durable, fire-resistive and low-maintenance, unlike plywood or fiber-cement boards. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated, Ch. 5 (Masonry Walls); Time-Saver Standards for Building Types (Industrial).

q: Which office arrangement should not be applied in order to lessen distractions?
o: Office Tables facing a window w/ a VIEW
n: Desks facing one another put coworkers in each other's direct line of sight, which raises visual and acoustic distraction. Source: Time-Saver Standards for Interior Design (Office Planning); Panero & Zelnik, Human Dimension and Interior Space.

q: For a Dining Chair, what is the standard height of the seat?
n: Standard dining chair seat height is about 430–460 mm, so 450 mm. Source: Panero & Zelnik, Human Dimension and Interior Space; Neufert, Architects' Data.

q: Handrails installed above steps or ramps shall have a minimum height of
n: BP 344 requires handrails on ramps and stairs at 900 mm above the surface (with a lower rail at 700 mm). Source: BP 344 (Accessibility Law) IRR, Rule II – Handrails; BP 344 2024 Revised IRR.

q: A recently married young couple, Rey and Vicky, moved into Rey's old apartment unit on the 2nd floor. However, when Vicky brought her things, which included a piano, they found the unit a little constricted. Being an architect, Rey thought of a nice solution: he decided, and got permits, to renovate the place and introduce a WINDOW that will bring in more natural light and create a little extra space for his wife's piano. What kind of window will he install?
n: A bow window is a curved bay that projects beyond the wall. It admits more daylight and adds usable floor space inside, such as an alcove for a piano. Source: Ching, A Visual Dictionary of Architecture (Window); Ching, Building Construction Illustrated, Ch. 8.

q: In estimating, the value 2.88 is used for
n: A 4 ft × 8 ft plywood sheet is taken as 1.20 m × 2.40 m = 2.88 sqm in estimates. Source: Max Fajardo, Simplified Construction Estimate (Plywood and Formworks).

q: A "look-up" plan.
n: A reflected ceiling plan shows the ceiling as if mirrored onto the floor below, i.e., a "look-up" plan. Source: Ching, Architectural Graphics (Plans – Reflected Ceiling Plans).

q: A parcel of land (Lot 4-B-20) in Sampaloc, Manila, is bounded on the W by Calle Cayco, on the N by Lot 4-B-19, on the E by Lot 4-B-21, and on the S by Calle Lepanto. Its technical description reads: beginning at point 1, thence N., 50 m to point 2; thence E., 100 m to point 3; thence S., 50 m to point 4; thence W., 100 m to the point of beginning. The property slopes 8% towards Calle Lepanto. From the given technical description, what is the TLA?
n: The technical description closes a rectangle: N 50 m, E 100 m, S 50 m, W 100 m. TLA = 50 × 100 = 5,000 sqm. Source: basic surveying (area from a closed traverse); Land Registration Authority technical description conventions.

q: An interior subdividing wall, such as that between bedrooms, is called?
n: A partition is an interior wall that subdivides spaces within a building, such as the wall between bedrooms. Source: Ching, A Visual Dictionary of Architecture (Wall).

q: A process of removing paint from walls with the use of chemicals.
n: Stripping is the removal of old paint with chemical removers (strippers). Scraping, sanding and heating are mechanical or thermal methods. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (Finishes); Harris, Dictionary of Architecture and Construction.
